This page maps measurement goals to the application's live and offline
workflows. Start with the goal, then follow the linked specialist guide for
configuration details and interpretation limits.

## Choose a workflow

| Goal | Start here | Primary result | Important limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Check a detector signal and acquire a spectrum | Scope **Auto Setup**, then MCA | Live waveform and accumulated pulse-height spectrum | Raw ADC and MCA channels are not physical units |
| Monitor a slowly changing sensor or detector current | Current: **IIR polling** or **Scope DMA** | Rolling calibrated trend and diagnostics | IIR and DMA are different raw signals and need separate calibration |
| Calibrate energy and quantify photopeaks | **Tools -> MCA Energy Calibration...**, then **MCA Peak Analysis Workbench...** | Applied channel-to-keV mapping and PDF/CSV/JSON fit reports | A two-point fit does not independently prove detector linearity |
| Measure detector response against a known dose rate | **Tools -> Dose Calibration Logger...** | Interval CSV with committed dose reference and selected observables | The logger records inputs; it does not certify or apply a dose-conversion model |
| Separate pulse populations | Live PSD, **PSD Event Readback**, or **Waveform Analysis Workbench** | PSD matrix, fitted figure of merit, and optional report bundle | Fit quality and stable acquisition settings must be checked before comparing FOM values |
| Measure two-channel timing or prompt coincidences | Coincidence workspace | Timing distribution, gated spectra, and prompt/random/corrected energy matrices | Both channels must belong to one physical digitizer |
| Investigate gain drift during startup | `examples/mca_gain_drift_diagnostic.py` | Time-series CSV/NPZ/JSON/PNG diagnostic bundle | It is a diagnostic trace, not an automatic gain correction |
| Reproduce an observed run without hardware | Session recording and **Replay Session...** | Integrity-checked `.nlab-session` bundle and deterministic analysis replay | Replay cannot recreate unrecorded device state or analogue conditions |
| Analyse existing files without connecting a board | **Offline / Replay Mode** | Waveform, PSD, spectrum, calibration, timing, and report workbenches | Offline analysis cannot start acquisition or modify hardware |
| Observe independent boards in one window | **Connection -> Add Digitizer...** | Channels labelled by board and independent per-board controls | Adding boards does not create cross-board clock synchronization |

## Detector checkout and pulse-height measurement

Use this path when bringing up a detector, checking polarity, or collecting a
first MCA spectrum:

1. Verify the IIO endpoint and physical channel identity.
2. Keep Scope DMA off and run Scope **Auto Setup**, or load trigger and DAC
   values qualified for that detector path.
3. Inspect a fresh waveform and stop Scope before handing ownership to another
   workflow.
4. Start MCA accumulation. Use the accumulated view for the final spectrum;
   the per-refresh differential view is for monitoring newly added counts.
5. Show the MCA ROI and double-click it when a count-history trace is useful.
   Moving the ROI or changing accumulated/differential mode begins a new trace.
6. Stop MCA before treating the chunked histogram as a stable snapshot.

The bottom MCA axis remains raw channel. The logarithmic display and the `L`
shortcut change presentation only. See [Getting Started](getting_started) and
[Acquisition Workflows](acquisition_workflows).

The stopped live view below is CH0 on `192.168.10.135:30431` with a CAEN
generator supplying artificial Na-22 test signals. It illustrates the retained
histogram, processing controls, statistics, and debug waveform without using
the PSU; it is not a radioactive-source measurement.

![Stopped live MCA view with the generated 511 and 1274.5 keV test lines and
the acquisition settings visible.](images/mca-na22-generator-ch0-live.png)

## Energy calibration and quantitative peak fitting

Use a stopped or explicitly labelled non-atomic MCA snapshot. In the energy
calibration workspace, draggable markers are *seeds*: each seed starts a local
Gaussian-plus-linear-background fit, and the fitted centroid becomes the
calibration coordinate. Inspect local count residuals and convergence before
applying a linear or quadratic mapping.

An applied calibration adds a keV top axis without changing raw bins, ROI
coordinates, or list-mode records. The **ENERGY CALIBRATED** badge identifies
the affected channels; a relevant DSP change marks the mapping stale.

For peak quantification, copy the calibrated spectrum into the peak-analysis
workbench, choose a fit interval and background model, and inspect residuals,
uncertainties, boundary warnings, and fit statistics together. The offline
radionuclide catalogue can suggest reference lines inside the explicit fit ROI,
but a matching line is not an isotope identification. Downloaded report
bundles retain plots, numerical tables, equations, provenance, and the exact
reference overlay. See [Analysis Tools](analysis_tools).

![Applied two-point calibration of the live generator spectrum with local
centroid fits and observed-minus-fit residuals.](images/mca-energy-calibration-na22-live.png)

## Dose-response data collection

Use the dose-calibration logger when a known source, geometry, and reference
dose rate must be recorded beside detector response and environmental state.
The expected dose and source label are committed only after editing finishes,
so timer-driven rows never capture a partially typed reference.

Selectable columns include MCA count rate and dead time, per-refresh total and
ROI integrals derived from accumulated spectra, bias setpoints/readbacks,
detector and board temperatures, and cumulative PSD integrals above/below the
cut. Missing live values remain blank. Each row is flushed immediately and an
existing file is never overwritten.

The adjacent plot is an operator aid over the bounded in-memory history; the
CSV is the record. Preserve source identity, geometry, shielding, detector
settings, stabilization time, and the independent reference-instrument record
when deriving a dose calibration. See [Analysis Tools](analysis_tools).

This live functional example deliberately records `0 µSv/h` for the CAEN
generator and disables PSU-dependent fields. It demonstrates logger and plot
behaviour, not a dose conversion.

![Dose logger after eight live MCA rows from the generator, with only MCA
statistics and differential integrals enabled.](images/dose-calibration-na22-generator-live.png)

## Pulse-shape-discrimination study

Choose the entry path based on the available data:

- **Live PSD** for immediate feedback from MCA charge-comparison events;
- **PSD Event Readback** for NDMA, CAEN, HDF5, or ROOT list-mode data;
- **Waveform Analysis Workbench** when short/long integrals must be rebuilt
  from NLab or CAEN waveforms.

Set the energy ROI before comparing populations. The ratio projection supports
a bounded two-Gaussian fit with draggable centroid seeds and a fit ROI. Treat
the reported FOM as qualified only when the convergence state, residuals,
widths, bounds, and reduced Poisson deviance are acceptable.

Waveform analysis can search short- and long-gate endpoints for a local FOM
maximum while holding the baseline, integration start, ROIs, and centroid seeds
fixed. This is a bounded local optimization, not proof of a globally optimal or
portable detector setting. Report bundles preserve the source path, matrix,
projections, separated spectra, fit components, settings, integration gates,
and machine-readable metadata. See [Live Pulse-Shape Discrimination](pulse_shape_discrimination)
and [Analysis Tools](analysis_tools).

![Completed live PSD capture with two generator populations, fitted component
curves, FOM values, and the poor-fit warning kept visible.](images/psd-ch0-live.png)

## Coincidence and timing measurement

Use Coincidence for two list-mode channels that share one digitizer's timing
and software-start core. Set MCA energy ROIs, select the logic mode, confirm the
timing convention, and inspect continuity before interpreting pair counts.

The energy matrix can show prompt, delayed-random, or corrected content. Raw
channels remain the primary axes; valid MCA calibrations add energy labels.
Exported HDF5/ROOT matrices retain gates, timing settings, calibration metadata,
and session diagnostics. Low-count transparency changes display only, not
matrix values or projections. See [Coincidence Measurement](coincidence).

![Live prompt coincidence energy matrix with both MCA gates and projections
visible.](images/coincidence-na22-511-matrix-live.png)

## Stability and gain-drift investigation

Use `examples/mca_gain_drift_diagnostic.py` when a known photopeak must be
tracked during startup, thermal settling, or a controlled bias study. The tool
reproduces saved MCA and ADC-temperature-correction settings, tracks the raw
maximum and a local centroid in separate channel ROIs, and logs available
temperature, power, rail, clock, MCA, and HV telemetry.

The script does not write Scope registers. Applying saved PSU bias requires the
explicit `--apply-saved-psu` option and guarantees safe shutdown cleanup; keep
an external supply's own log when detector bias is not controlled by the
digitizer. Compare repeated runs using the emitted CSV, NPZ, JSON, and PNG
artifacts rather than a screenshot alone.

## Reproducible capture and offline review

Start session recording before the measurements of interest. Recording is
passive: it observes existing Scope, MCA, Current, list-mode, telemetry, and log
streams without starting acquisition. A finalized `.nlab-session` bundle
contains configuration, committed stream counts, integrity hashes, a timeline,
and mutable analysis annotations.

Open **Offline / Replay Mode** when no board should be contacted. Session replay
validates finalized content and rebuilds recorded views from one replay clock;
standalone file workbenches remain available without loading a session. Use
**Connection -> Connect...** later to replace the offline workspace with a live
one only after every requested channel validates successfully.

Replay is suitable for review, report generation, training, and deterministic
software comparisons. It is not a hardware simulator and does not resend
recorded commands. See [Capture Files and Integrity](data_formats) and the
session section in the project [README](https://github.com/nucliflare/nlab-digitizer-community#session-recording-and-deterministic-analysis-replay).

## Multi-digitizer observation

Use **Connection -> Add Digitizer...** to place independent boards in one live
workspace. Channels are labelled `D1:CH0`, `D1:CH1`, `D2:CH0`, and so on;
global diagnostics and shared-start controls remain per board. Resolved IP
addresses prevent the same endpoint being added again through a hostname alias.

This workflow is appropriate for consolidated monitoring and independent
acquisition. It does not imply a shared clock. Coincidence pairs remain limited
to two eligible channels on the same selected digitizer. Disconnecting the last
board returns the application to offline analysis mode.
